resources.string: Applies one set of switches at a time; individual switches below can override

string-array.name: tier_entries
string-array.item: Minimal (keep current state; make no changes to the system)
Standard (AGPS off + ad framework off + location device only + scans off + NFC off)
Strict (Standard + captive portal check off + USB adb off + auto time off)
Custom (not applied automatically; adjust the switches below manually)

resources.string: Opens the system per-app language screen; English is the default and the app follows the system language by default.
View / adjust each app\'s camera, microphone and location permissions (handled by the platform UI)
stats_collection=0 disables it; tree default is enabled
The system no longer automatically connects to check whether the gateway is hijacking traffic. Side effect: public Wi-Fi login pages will not pop up automatically, so open the browser manually.
Uses a DNS-over-TLS hostname. Side effect: DNS fails when that host is unavailable.

When off, the system no longer downloads the Qualcomm XTRA almanac (no longer connects to time.xtracloud.net). Affects network assistance only; standalone GPS still works; emergency calls force it on. Verify: adb shell settings get global assisted_gps_enabled
When off, plugging in USB no longer automatically enables the adb debug channel. Verify: adb shell settings get global adb_enabled
Leave empty to use the system default (AOSP defaults to pool.ntp.org). You can enter a self-hosted or LAN NTP server to reduce external connections. Verify: adb shell settings get global ntp_server
When off, the system no longer corrects the time via NTP / the carrier network (fewer external queries). Side effect: the time must be set manually. Verify: adb shell settings get global auto_time
Off writes location_mode=0 (location fully disabled). On writes the accuracy selected below. Verify: adb shell settings get secure location_mode
When off, scanning no longer continues even with Wi-Fi off (scan results can be used to estimate location). Verify: adb shell settings get global wifi_scan_always_enabled
When off, Bluetooth Low Energy scanning no longer continues (can be used for proximity estimation). Verify: adb shell settings get global ble_scan_always_enabled

This switch is owned by the platform (the camera/microphone Quick Settings tiles). This app cannot hold the required permission: MANAGE_SENSOR_PRIVACY protectionLevel is internal|installer|role, so neither the privileged allowlist nor a platform signature grants it. Tapping opens the system privacy settings instead. Verify: adb shell dumpsys sensor_privacy
Why this app does not provide the camera/microphone switch

The software on/off state for camera/microphone lives in SensorPrivacyService\'s PersistedState XML, not as a Settings row, and changing it needs MANAGE_SENSOR_PRIVACY (protectionLevel internal|installer|role). A privileged platform-signed app is not granted it either, so any local toggle would silently do nothing. The app therefore links to the platform privacy screen, which is the only place that owns the state.
When off, nearby NFC tags / sensing are no longer read (smaller passive exposure surface). Verify: adb shell settings get global nfc_on
AOSP includes com.android.adservices (advertising APIs such as Topics / FLEDGE). Disabled by default. Verify: adb shell device_config get adservices adservice_enabled
Persistent logcatd (write logs to disk at boot) status
Why logcatd can only show status

This app is currently not in the system_app domain, so SELinux does not allow writing directly to persist.logd.logpersistd. To toggle it from within the app, add set_prop(system_app, logpersistd_logging_prop) to the device sepolicy and run this app as android.uid.system. Here it intentionally only shows status and does not provide a fake switch.
Read-only notes (cannot be changed in the app)

ro.* properties can only be set at build time. Current value: adb shell getprop ro.adb.secure (0 = no authorization on USB plug-in, less secure; for the privacy build it is recommended to set 1 at build time)
Vendor telemetry components (diagzn / psiclient / wifilearner / perfd)

Class C: started as an init service; stopping it at runtime requires root. The approach is to remove it from the blob copy list at privacy-build time; after removal, verify calls / mobile data / signal on a real device.

Class C (/proc/sys writes require root). Current state on this device: dmesg_restrict=0 (any app can read the kernel log), perf_event_paranoid=-1 (performance events fully open). For the privacy build it is recommended to set 1 and 2/3 at build time. Verify: adb shell cat /proc/sys/kernel/dmesg_restrict

org.lineageos.updater exists and queries the LineageOS API for new versions (an external connection). There is currently no runtime switch; you can disable that app in system settings, or have the privacy build remove it.

Measured on this device, connections use a randomized MAC (useRandomizedMac=true), and the hardware supports CONNECTED_RAND_MAC. This is a positive current state, so no switch is needed. Verify: adb shell dumpsys wifi | grep -i mac

Class C: a Google proprietary APEX with no runtime disable mechanism. The cost of removal is that DRM playback such as Netflix / Disney+ stops working. It is recommended to ship two variants and let the user choose.
Every switch maps to a real system setting; each summary includes a reproducible adb verification command.
